source_evidence.text:
You can also call `retry()` to explicitly force a message to be redelivered in a subsequent batch. This is referred to as "negative acknowledgement". This can be particularly useful when you want to process the rest of the messages in that batch without throwing an error that would force the entire batch to be redelivered.

You can also acknowledge or negatively acknowledge messages at a batch level with `ackAll()` and `retryAll()`. Calling `ackAll()` on the batch of messages (`MessageBatch`) delivered to your consumer Worker has the same behaviour as a consumer Worker that successfully returns (does not throw an error).

Note that calls to `ack()`, `retry()` and their `ackAll()` / `retryAll()` equivalents follow the below precedence rules:

- If you call `ack()` on a message, subsequent calls to `ack()` or `retry()` are silently ignored.
- If you call `retry()` on a message and then call `ack()`: the `ack()` is ignored. The first method call wins in all cases.

source_evidence.text:
GET /objects/:id is deliberately public, including the R2 public content. A capability holder may create objects and replace their own existing objects. Capabilities expire at expiresAt (Unix milliseconds); expired capabilities must not write. Existing objects owned by another subject must not be overwritten.
GET /mint only proposes a random token and record. Operators review proposals out of band, choose a real subject and finite future expiresAt, and manually insert approved records into CAPS (a Workers KV namespace); the Worker never activates its proposals. Possessing a proposal alone grants no write access. All records in CAPS have a nonempty string sub and finite numeric expiresAt. Stale KV state after manual revocation is an accepted documented operational limitation, not a guarantee of immediate revocation.
BUCKET is R2. Existing objects have customMetadata.owner containing the subject. Object ids are 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. Content is public static text and has no confidentiality requirement. Metadata ownership is still enforced for writes. There are no other code paths or external authorization checks.
An upstream per-object lock serializes all PUT invocations to the same key through completion; same-key writes cannot overlap. This lock provides no authentication or owner check.

KV achieves high performance by [caching ↗︎](https://www.cloudflare.com/en-gb/learning/cdn/what-is-caching/) which makes reads eventually-consistent with writes.

Changes are usually immediately visible in the Cloudflare global network location at which they are made. Changes may take up to 60 seconds or more to be visible in other global network locations as their cached versions of the data time out.
